answer: Through the fable, the economy stays open to anyone willing to pay the price of entry, and closed to free clones. Reputation is not permanent: every identity's standing decays each epoch unless refreshed by fresh, attested work. The horizon rule means a farm cannot season a thousand clones once and coast — each one needs continuous real contributions, and idle fakes slide back to zero. Through the copper, one real agent costs once and a thousand pretenders cost a thousand times — no shortcut survives that math.
